title: Accessible care for adults with autism spectrum disorder through multi-professional autism teams (BASS-Teams)
summary:
Adults on the autism spectrum frequently encounter barriers when accessing healthcare services (e.g., at treatment or consultation appointments). These barriers are not necessarily visible from the outside, but may include difficulties in communicating with healthcare professionals, processing environmental stimuli, or carrying out necessary steps (e.g., filling prescriptions). In the worst case, such barriers result in autistic individuals not receiving the care they urgently require. Reducing these barriers calls for measures that help people with autism to communicate their barriers, as well as measures that raise awareness among healthcare professionals and prompt them to make their services as accessible as possible for autistic individuals.

The research project aims to introduce the BASS-Teams treatment model in the pilot regions of Hamburg, Cologne, and Munich. Through adapted structural conditions (e.g., reduced environmental stimuli, designated contact persons, more detailed information about procedures), the model seeks to establish greater accessibility within healthcare services, particularly in the areas of diagnostics and counselling or treatment. Treatment within BASS-Teams can vary in intensity and is overseen by a designated case manager. Counselling or treatment is then delivered either by staff within the BASS-Teams treatment team (e.g., social workers, physicians, psychotherapists) or by healthcare professionals within the BASS-Teams competence network (e.g., counselling centres, self-help groups).

To evaluate whether the BASS-Teams treatment model offers advantages over standard care, a concurrent scientific study is being conducted with autistic individuals. The study will involve a total of 326 autistic adults. Participants will complete various questionnaires in online surveys and take part in brief interviews. Data will be collected at three time points in total: at baseline and after six and 12 months. Following the initial data collection, study participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups: the intervention group receives the BASS-Teams treatment model for 12 months, while the control group continues to receive standard care for the same period. The care situation for the control group therefore remains unchanged. At the end of the study, the two groups (intervention group and control group) will be examined to see if they differ with respect to various outcome criteria after 12 months, such as perceived barriers, quality of life, functional impairment in daily activities, number of services utilized, and costs to the healthcare system.

In order to investigate the feasibility of implementing the BASS-Teams treatment model, in addition to participants in the intervention group, 55 close relatives of participants and 54 healthcare professionals are surveyed at three time points regarding their assessment of the BASS treatment model. This approach is intended to capture a wide range of perspectives.

interventions.name: Intervention Group (BASS-Teams Treatment Model): Adults with a confirmed diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) receive access to the BASS-Teams treatment model for 12 months (the frequency of individual treatment services varies).
Active Control Group (Care as Usual): Adults with a confirmed diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) receive care as usual for 12 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). Inclusion criteria are: written documentation of a substantiated suspected diagnosis or confirmed diagnosis of autism spectrum disorder (e.g., ICD-10: F84.0, F84.1, F84.5), issued by a specialist physician in psychiatry and psychotherapy or a licensed psychological psychotherapist (or similar qualified person); place of residence within a maximum of 1.5 hour travel time (by public transport) from the respective regional BASS treatment team site; enrolment in a German statutory health insurance scheme; sufficient language proficiency (German).
Exclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of intellectual disability (e.g., ICD-10: F71, F72, F73); diagnosis of an organic mental disorder (z. B. ICD-10: F00-F09); participation of another household member in the RCT study; participation in another intervention study (currently or less than three months ago).
